Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Arvind Kumar Pathak
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
No one has appeared for the complainant.
2. The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was in love with the applicant.
She also admitted physical relations with the applicant.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she changed her version and alleged that she was taken away by the applicant without her wishes.

There is no concrete evidence with regard to the age of the victim and reliance has been placed on the transfer certificate by the prosecution which cannot be said to be a conclusive evidence with regard to age,

1 which shall be determined at the time of trial.
A supplementary affidavit has been filed today, which is taken on record, annexing therewith photograph of the victim and the applicant which suggests that there was proximity in between them.
3. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

4. Considering the submissions made at the Bar coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 23.06.2022 and has no criminal antecedent, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Jitendra Kumar be released on bail in FIR No.140 of 2022, under Section 363,
366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, P.S. Khandasa, District Faizabad/Ayodhya on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
